Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for evaluating this young male patient, whom I saw in consultation today for an ongoing clinical appraisal.

His parents initially sought assessment due to notable scholastic struggles. Comprehensive educational evaluation recently demonstrated an isolated learning difficulty centered on written expression and reading. Otherwise, his early developmental history has been reassuring; his parents confirm that his speech acquisition and early language milestones progressed entirely on time, without any delays. He is physically active, currently takes no prescription medications, and has an unremarkable family history.

On physical examination, he appears bright and interactive. His head circumference plots neatly along the 50th percentile, showing no cranial enlargement. A thorough dermatological survey reveals several smooth-edged, light-brown hyperpigmented patches scattered across his abdomen and thighs, each measuring greater than a centimeter. I carefully inspected the flexural areas, and his axillary vaults were completely clear of any small lentigines or clustered macules. Furthermore, palpation of his extremities and torso demonstrated smooth soft tissues with no subcutaneous fatty lumps or lipomatous nodules. Neurological screening, including cranial nerves, gross motor coordination, and deep tendon reflexes, was completely normal, and cardiopulmonary auscultation was unremarkable.

Given the combination of cutaneous findings and his academic profile, I would be most grateful for your formal assessment and recommendations regarding appropriate next steps.

Warm regards,

Dr. Laura Bennett
General Pediatrics
